resolutions.action: Option A. A `Title and body at birth (both paths — never improvised)` paragraph in PR_PROPOSE_SECTION: titles passed EXPLICITLY (`gh pr create` without `--title` prompts) — per-change `<change-name>: <proposal.md's title line>`, program `<doc stem>: <doc title line>`; per-change body = intent adapted from Why/What; program body = program intent adapted from the doc's opening prose (before the first `### Stage`) plus its stage list; titles set ONCE at birth, the tail's rewrite/append touch the body only. The mid-flight recovery `gh pr create` command now carries `--title` and `--body-file`. The orbit-pr-lifecycle landmark requirement gained the title-once and program-body-at-birth clauses.

resolutions.title: Stage-entry APPEND has no read-current-body step; `gh pr edit --body-file` REPLACES, so a literal performance wipes earlier stages' entries
resolutions.action: PR_ARCHIVE_TAIL_SECTION gained `APPEND means READ-APPEND-WRITE`: read the current body (`gh pr view --repo <owner>/<repo> <url> --json body -q .body`), append this stage's entry, write the COMPOSED whole; writing only the entry would destroy every earlier stage's entry — the landmark itself. The recovery bullet says the file is the composed body, never the entry alone. The landmark requirement in the orbit-pr-lifecycle delta states the read-append-write rule. The new `gh pr view` invocation is repository-qualified (fidelity test passes).

resolutions.title: The attachment record (propose emit) is written AFTER the phase-3 push and rides no D6-guaranteed push until archive — a fresh checkout between seams silently loses the attachment and the PR is stranded draft
resolutions.action: Option A. The reference's `Recording the attachment` section ends with `Then COMMIT and PUSH the record — the seam's final act`: stage exactly the emit file, commit, push to the resolved remote; same seam, same invocation, no new consent, the only push between propose and archive (seams-only rule untouched); a failure is a mid-flight failure naming the completing command. Both bodies' emit steps say the emit is not the last act when the choreography ran. The orbit-propose-modifications delta's phase-3 description carries the step and a new scenario `The attachment record reaches the branch`. Chose A because the tail's correctness rests entirely on that record and the choreography already owns push at this seam.

resolutions.title: Design's mid-flight-adoption risk bullet is inaccurate for this repo: the program branch is named by doc stem, and `d-arc` is not `d-arc-arbitered-flow`
resolutions.action: The Risks bullet now states adoption covers only a branch already carrying the stem name: enabling per-architecture here would not adopt `d-arc` — phase 1 would create `d-arc-arbitered-flow` off the resolved default, cutting the worktree to main's tree; adoption needs a rename or the deferred override. It also names the per-proposal consequence: a standalone change proposed from `d-arc` gets its branch cut from `origin/main`. The proposal's Dogfood bullet gained the matching caveat (run the dogfood once main carries the d-arc work, or from a checkout whose default is the intended base) — an operational note the user should read before exit criterion 1.

resolutions.title: Surface the HEAD-mismatch observation at archive ENTRY, not only in the post-move tail
resolutions.action: Archive Step 5.45 (read-only preflight) now also observes whether HEAD's branch equals `pr_attachment.branch` and, on mismatch, says so in the consent preview when one fires and otherwise as one line BEFORE any archive write, naming both branches — so the user can switch first instead of carrying uncommitted sync/move/emit writes across a `git switch`. The reference's HEAD precondition notes the early observation and remains the guard.

resolutions.title: Define "this change's own artifact commits" for per-proposal compatibility
resolutions.action: Step 5's per-proposal compatibility is now a PATH test, never a commit-message test: every path `git diff --name-only <remote>/<default>...<branch>` lists is under `orbit/changes/<change-name>/` (or a deletion under `orbit/explore/<change-name>/`); any other path is a collision, skip naming the foreign path. The transcription replaces the subject-contains-branch heuristic with the same diff filter and names the first foreign path in its note; the harness collision case asserts the named path (`unrelated.md`).

resolutions.title: Propose's commit-scope prohibition on directory prefixes is stricter than the archive's, for the same kind of orbit-created directory
resolutions.action: The propose commit scope is now an explicit file set — proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, every specs/<capability>/spec.md, `.openspec.yaml` (named with the reason: it carries the stamped base fingerprints), the moved staging material (explore.md, sketches, the moved `.orbit-runs/` trail files — listed), and the staging-directory deletions — with the `-A` / bare-prefix prohibition kept. Chose the explicit list over a symmetric prefix exception because the two forgettable files are exactly the ones a prefix would silently include or a hurried enumeration would miss; naming them is the safer form.

resolutions.title: Step 5.8 echo is unspecified for the attached-but-positively-invalidated archive
resolutions.action: Step 5.8 gained the clause: after a tail whose PR half was SKIPPED on positive invalidation (commit and push landed; rewrite/append and flip did not), name the specific reason and that any action on that pull request is the user's.
